---
title: "Glossary"
subtitle: "The words the course uses, and where they first come up."
---

::: {.glossary}

Acceleration
: How fast a body's velocity changes, in pixels per second per second. Low acceleration feels heavy. [Lesson 4](lessons/04-physics.qmd#acceleration-and-drag)

Animation
: A list of frames from a spritesheet and a speed to play them at. Made once with `this.anims.create`, shared by the whole game. [Lesson 5](lessons/05-assets.qmd#make-an-animation)

Arcade physics
: Phaser's fast, simple physics engine: boxes and circles that don't rotate. The one this course uses. Compare *Matter*. [Lesson 4](lessons/04-physics.qmd)

Atlas
: One image packed with frames of different sizes, plus a JSON file naming each frame. The efficient alternative to many separate images. [Lesson 5](lessons/05-assets.qmd#what-the-loader-can-load)

Body
: What the physics engine sees of a game object: a box with a position, velocity and size. Not always the same size as the picture. [Lesson 4](lessons/04-physics.qmd#bodies-and-game-objects)

Callback
: A function you hand to something else to call later: when two bodies touch, when a timer ends, when a tween finishes. [Lesson 1](lessons/01-javascript.qmd#the-one-thing-about-this)

Camera
: What decides which part of the world is on screen. Every scene has one; you can add more. [Lesson 6](lessons/06-worlds.qmd#a-camera-that-follows)

Collider
: A rule that two things are solid to each other: Phaser pushes them apart, and can call you back. Compare *overlap*. [Lesson 4](lessons/04-physics.qmd#collide-or-overlap)

Core loop
: The short thing a player does over and over. In *Cold Chain*: pick up, cross the lab, store. [Lesson 8](lessons/08-mechanics.qmd#the-core-loop)

Delta
: The time since the last frame, in milliseconds. Multiply speeds by it so a game runs the same at any frame rate. [Lesson 0](lessons/00-engine.qmd#frames-arent-all-the-same-length)

Depth
: Draw order. Higher depth draws on top. [Lesson 2](lessons/02-first-scene.qmd#draw-order)

Dominant strategy
: One choice that's always best, so players stop choosing. A design bug. [Lesson 8](answers/08-mechanics-answers.qmd#ex-8.2)

Drag
: How fast a body slows down when nothing's pushing it. In Arcade physics it only acts on an axis with no acceleration. [Lesson 4](lessons/04-physics.qmd#acceleration-and-drag)

Dynamic body
: A body that moves and can be pushed. Players, carts. Compare *static body*. [Lesson 4](lessons/04-physics.qmd#static-and-dynamic)

Ease
: How a tween travels from start to end: steadily, fast then slow, overshooting, bouncing. [Lesson 9](lessons/09-feel.qmd#eases)

Frame
: (1) One pass of the game loop, about 1/60 of a second. (2) One picture in a spritesheet. [Lesson 0](lessons/00-engine.qmd#a-game-is-a-loop), [lesson 2](lessons/02-first-scene.qmd#load-the-files)

Game feel
: Fast, physical feedback (tweens, particles, shake, sound) that makes actions feel like they matter. Also called *juice*. [Lesson 9](lessons/09-feel.qmd)

Game loop
: Read input, update the world, draw the frame, repeat. [Lesson 0](lessons/00-engine.qmd#a-game-is-a-loop)

Game object
: Anything a scene can show: an image, a sprite, text, a tilemap layer. Made with `this.add`. [Lesson 2](lessons/02-first-scene.qmd#put-things-on-the-screen)

Group
: A collection of similar game objects that share settings and can collide as one. [Lesson 4](lessons/04-physics.qmd#static-and-dynamic)

Hit-stop
: Freezing the action for a few milliseconds when something hits, so the impact feels heavy. [Lesson 9](lessons/09-feel.qmd#getting-hit)

HUD
: Heads-up display: the meters, counters and clock drawn over the game. *Cold Chain*'s is its own scene. [Lesson 7](lessons/07-scenes.qmd#the-registry-shared-data)

Lerp
: Short for *linear interpolation*. For a camera: how much of the gap to its target it closes each frame. [Lesson 6](lessons/06-worlds.qmd#a-camera-that-follows)

Loader
: `this.load`: queues files in `preload()` and loads them before `create()`. [Lesson 5](lessons/05-assets.qmd)

localStorage
: The browser's small key-and-text store, kept per site. How games remember things between visits. [Lesson 10](lessons/10-ship.qmd#remember-things)

Matter
: Phaser's other physics engine: rotating shapes, stacking, joints. Slower and harder to control than Arcade. [Lesson 4](lessons/04-physics.qmd#where-you-start)

Object layer
: A layer in a Tiled map that holds points and shapes instead of tiles: where things start, with properties. [Lesson 6](lessons/06-worlds.qmd#put-things-on-the-map)

Origin
: The point of a game object that sits at its `x, y`. The middle for images; the top-left for text. [Lesson 2](lessons/02-first-scene.qmd#where-things-go)

Overlap
: A rule that tells you when two things touch, without pushing them apart. For pickups and zones. [Lesson 4](lessons/04-physics.qmd#collide-or-overlap)

Particle emitter
: Spawns many short-lived images (frost, dust, sparks), continuously or in bursts. [Lesson 9](lessons/09-feel.qmd#particles)

Pointer
: Phaser's name for a mouse or a finger. The same events work for both. [Lesson 10](lessons/10-ship.qmd#touch)

Registry
: A store of values shared by every scene, with an event when anything changes. [Lesson 7](lessons/07-scenes.qmd#the-registry-shared-data)

Risk and reward
: A choice where the better outcome costs something to reach. A real one is taken sometimes, not always. [Lesson 8](lessons/08-mechanics.qmd#risk-and-reward)

Scale Manager
: Fits the game's fixed size into the browser window. `FIT` is the safe default. [Lesson 10](lessons/10-ship.qmd#fit-any-screen)

Scene
: One screen of a game (a title, a level, a HUD), with its own objects and its own `preload`, `create` and `update`. [Lesson 2](lessons/02-first-scene.qmd#a-scene-and-its-lifecycle), [lesson 7](lessons/07-scenes.qmd)

Scroll factor
: How much an object moves with the camera. `0` pins it to the screen; between 0 and 1 gives parallax. [Lesson 6](lessons/06-worlds.qmd#things-that-dont-scroll)

Spritesheet
: One image cut into a grid of equal frames. [Lesson 5](lessons/05-assets.qmd#the-researcher-spritesheet)

Static body
: A body that never moves and can't be pushed. Walls, benches. Cheaper than a dynamic one. [Lesson 4](lessons/04-physics.qmd#static-and-dynamic)

Texture
: An image loaded into the game, by key. A missing key gives a green-outlined placeholder. [Lesson 2](lessons/02-first-scene.qmd#load-the-files)

Tile, tileset, tilemap
: A small square image; the image the tiles come from; a grid of tiles that makes a level. [Lesson 6](lessons/06-worlds.qmd)

Tuning file
: One file holding every number that changes how the game plays, so design can change without touching code. [Lesson 8](lessons/08-mechanics.qmd#tuning-as-data)

Tween
: Changes a property smoothly from one value to another over time. [Lesson 9](lessons/09-feel.qmd#tweens)

Velocity
: Speed and direction, in pixels per second. Set it on a body and physics moves it. [Lesson 4](lessons/04-physics.qmd#velocity-not-position)

Vite
: The tool behind `npm run dev` and `npm run build`: serves the game while you work, and bundles it to ship. [Lesson 1](lessons/01-javascript.qmd#npm-and-vite)

:::
